answer: Each newcomer must own one registered thoroughbred: the stud book ties one horse to one identity, papers checked live. One horse, one identity; shared stables fail at the gate, an island no script can duplicate. A fake costs $15,000 for the horse plus $200 monthly boarding for a year: $17,400 and 365 days, a spiral per fake. Cheapest dodge: a retired claimer for $4,000, but it has not raced in a season, so the live check voids it; a leased horse still names its owner, and a seller giving up papers loses their own backing. One horse, one name, one pearl: 100 fakes, $1,740,000 and 36,500 days.
